title: MYASTHENIC SYNDROME, CONGENITAL, 11, ASSOCIATED WITH ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: MYASTHENIC SYNDROME, CONGENITAL, 11, ASSOCIATED WITH ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 associated with acetylcholine receptor deficiency (CMS11) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding rapsyn (RAPSN).

checks.claim: Congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 associated with acetylcholine receptor deficiency (CMS11) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RAPSN gene, which encodes rapsyn.
checks.evidence_quote: we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5
checks.explanation: Recessive mutations in rapsyn, homozygous and compound heterozygous, cause endplate AChR deficiency CMS.

paragraphs.text: Congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 (CMS11) is an autosomal recessive disorder of neuromuscular transmission. It results from deficiency of the postsynaptic protein rapsyn, which clusters the acetylcholine receptor (AChR) at the motor endplate, and therefore causes endplate AChR deficiency (Ohno et al., 2002). Engel et al. (2015) stated that most patients present in the first year of life and a few later in life. Nearly one-third have arthrogryposis or other congenital malformations at birth, and intercurrent infections or fever can trigger respiratory crises. Most patients respond well to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (Engel et al., 2015).

paragraphs.text: Goldhammer et al. (1990) described 14 Jewish patients from 10 families of Iraqi or Iranian origin who had congenital myasthenia with facial malformations. The malformations included an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion, and a high-arched palate. Muscle weakness was mostly limited to ptosis, weakness of the facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech. The course was mild and nonprogressive. Patients responded to cholinesterase inhibitors and had no antibodies to the acetylcholine receptor. Repetitive stimulation at 3 Hz produced a decremental response, but a single nerve stimulus did not evoke a repetitive compound muscle action potential. The authors noted that the facial abnormalities might either result from the neuromuscular defect or be primary and unrelated to it.

paragraphs.text: Burke et al. (2003) identified 2 distinct phenotypes, early onset and late onset, among 16 unrelated patients with a congenital/hereditary myasthenic syndrome and rapsyn mutations. The late-onset phenotype developed in adolescence or adulthood and was at first mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.

paragraphs.text: Das et al. (2014) reported a 20-month-old boy with rapsyn deficiency. At birth he had a weak cry, hypotonia, joint contractures, and facial deformity. Because of respiratory difficulty associated with muscle fatigue, he spent a total of 71 days in the neonatal intensive care unit and 47 days in the pediatric intensive care unit. Imaging, metabolic tests, and electrodiagnostic studies were normal. A muscle biopsy showed myofiber atrophy in a pattern consistent with early denervation.

paragraphs.text: In a review, Engel et al. (2015) stated that the clinical features of rapsyn deficiency can suggest autoimmune myasthenia gravis, but ocular ductions are intact in most patients. Apneic episodes can occur. Endplate studies show multiple synaptic contacts on single muscle fibers and poorly differentiated junctional folds. The endplate AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2002) studied 4 patients with endplate AChR deficiency who had no mutations in AChR subunit genes and identified 3 recessive mutations in the RAPSN gene. One patient was compound heterozygous for L14P in tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) 1 and N88K in TPR3. Two patients were homozygous for N88K. One patient was compound heterozygous for N88K and a 5-bp insertion (553ins5) that causes a frameshift in TPR5. In expression studies in HEK cells, none of the mutations impaired rapsyn self-association, but all 3 reduced coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) identified 2 mutations in E-box sequences of the RAPSN promoter region in 8 patients with CMS. Patient 1 carried a -27C-G mutation, which changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. The allele carrying this mutation was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Patients 2 through 8 were Oriental Jews of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations. They carried a -38A-G mutation, which changes another E-box at -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG without altering the CANNTG consensus. In electrophoretic mobility shift assays, -38A-G gained binding affinity and -27C-G lost binding affinity for different components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. In luciferase reporter assays, both mutations reduced reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes.

paragraphs.text: Gaudon et al. (2010) studied 3 patients with a recessive CMS phenotype and RAPSN mutations. Familial analysis showed that direct sequencing had failed to detect one mutant allele in each. Allelic quantification of patient DNA identified 3 novel multiexon deletions of RAPSN. These rearrangements accounted for 15% of the authors' CMS patients with RAPSN mutations. The authors recommended single-nucleotide polymorphism markers and gene dosage analysis in addition to direct sequencing.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -27C-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter region in a patient with CMS (patient 1). The mutation changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. The allele carrying it was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. The mutation lost binding affinity for components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. It attenuated reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes and in HEK cells transfected with MyoD or myogenin, and it markedly attenuated the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter.
